How to use Slice Horn Lab

Draw the cabinet's side view as 18 mm / ¾" boards, set the width, drop in a driver, and it simulates it with a Hornresp-style 1-D model: SPL, impedance, excursion, group delay, step response, waterfall and max SPL.

Quick start

  1. It opens with an 18" tapped horn so you can see how it works. Start from (top) has more presets.
  2. Pick a driver at the top: filter by Brand and Size, or click the search box (or press /) and type a model, brand or size. It also takes neo, 8ohm and limits like fs<35, xmax>10, qts<0.4. Import driver… takes a Hornresp file, WinISD .wdr or a spec sheet PDF.
  3. Edit the cabinet here on the left. The curves update as you drag.
  4. Read the results on the tabs above the graph (SPL, Impedance, Excursion, Group delay, Step, Decay, Max SPL…).
  5. File → Download design saves your work. It also auto-saves in this browser.

Drawing

  • P draw a board (click-drag). Snaps to the grid, corners and faces. Grid units at the top: 1", 0.1", cm, mm.
  • V select. Drag a board's end to stretch it (joined ends follow; Shift = that end only), its middle to move it, anywhere else to slide it sideways. It clicks to square / 45° only right on the line; nudge sideways to leave it, or hold Alt to turn the angle snap off.
  • C curved board (bent ply): click its start, click its end, move to bend it and click. Drag the square end handles or the round bend handle to reshape it; select it to set an exact radius.
  • D driver: click a board to mount it. F flips it. Right-click it for front/rear mounting.
  • Right-click a corner to change how two boards join.
  • Cabinet width slider, pinned under the chart: how far the side view extends into the screen (driver + 1" to 2 × the driver). Every throat, mouth and port area and every chamber volume scales with it; the line under the slider shows them, and a dashed Before curve shows how far the response moved.
  • Design panel (right side, scroll down): board thickness, floor / wall / corner loading.
  • Air paths are found automatically. You don't need to draw them.
  • Ctrl Z undo · wheel zooms · right-drag pans · 0 fit · ? this help.

The 3-D view

  • The cube button in the toolbar shows a 3-D view beside the drawing: the boards extruded across the cabinet width, the side panels (see-through, so the fold shows) and the drivers with their cutouts. It follows the drawing as you edit.
  • Drag rotates it, Shift + drag pans, Ctrl + drag zooms, the wheel zooms. Click a board to select it in the drawing too.
  • Click a viewport's name for Wireframe / Shaded / Ghosted, solid or hidden side panels, Top / Front / Right views and a 4-viewport layout. Double-click the name to maximise that viewport, and again to restore.

Rhino-style controls (this computer only)

  • Controls (top bar) switches between Rhino and Classic. The keys under Drawing above are the Classic ones.
  • Command line: just start typing, then Enter or Space. M Move · Co Copy · Ro Rotate · Mi Mirror · L Line (a board) · PL Polyline (boards end to end) · Rec Rectangle (box shell) · ZS Zoom Selected · ZE Zoom Extents · U Undo · Di Distance · SelAll · 4View · MaxViewport. Enter, Space or a right-click repeats the last command; Esc cancels.
  • Exact sizes: while a command asks for a point, type a distance (24), a point (12,6), a relative point (r12,0 or @12,0), or an angle (<45, 24<45), in the grid's units.
  • Mouse: right-drag pans the drawing and rotates the Perspective view; Shift + right-drag pans, Ctrl + right-drag zooms, the wheel zooms. Click selects, Shift adds, Ctrl removes. Drag a box left-to-right for a window, right-to-left for a crossing selection.
  • Status bar: Grid Snap (F9), Ortho (F8, or hold Shift) and Osnap. Alt while dragging a board end moves that end only.

Handy extras

  • Power slider (left of the graph, 1 W–10 kW, on every tab): scales SPL, excursion and air velocity; anything past Xmax turns red.
  • DSP bar: HPF/LPF (Butterworth, LR, Bessel up to 48 dB/oct) + 6 PEQs, with the filter curve shown in green.
  • Target: drag orange EQ-style handles to the response you want, then Auto-tune re-design reshapes the cabinet to match.
  • Pin curve to compare before and after.
  • Quantize the build (Design panel) rounds everything to whole mm and 5° angles before you cut.
  • Export: cut list, DXF side profile, CSV response, and the equivalent Hornresp inputs to cross-check.
  • Presets: 18" tapped horn (Speaker Box Maker), 1850 folded horn (Rog Mogale), SKRAM 21" and Skhorn 2×21" (Josh Ricci), BC118 (All_1), Super Scooper 18" and 21", 186 Horn, HD 15 Horn, G Sub and X1 (Rog Mogale), S12BP, S21HL and S218BP (B&C Speakers), plus tapped horn / FLH / vented / sealed templates.

Limits

It's a 1-D plane-wave model like Hornresp (checked against Hornresp exports: 0.00 dB on a front-loaded horn, ~0.05 dB on a vented box). It doesn't model panel flex, port compression or driver non-linearity, so treat the red over-excursion areas as "not actually reachable". The preset designs are traced approximations for simulation; build from the designers' own plans.

Full manual and source: github.com/SpPank/slice-horn-lab
